									<p>Each year the Freedom Festival Essay Contest gives rise to expressions of patriotism from students in K-12th grades throughout the nation. …This year’s theme is “We Hold These Truths to be Self Evident,” as we celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. Students may choose to illustrate the purposes and applications of the Declaration of Independence that may include its history, adoption, and recognition of significant individuals involved. Or they may focus on any concept or specific freedom that shaped our nation included in the Declaration of Independence. Submission deadline is March 1, 2026. </p><p>The phrase “We hold these truths” is one of the most powerful lines ever written in American history and it still speaks to us today. These words remind us that the ideas of freedom, equality, and human rights are not just for the past – they continue to shape who we are and what we believe in. Students should explore what those truths mean, how they have guided the nation, how it is relevant in their own life, and how people though history have worked to make them real for everyo<span style="font-style: inherit; font-weight: inherit;">ne. </span></p>								</div>

									<p>This year’s theme is “We Hold These Truths to be Self Evident” Students may choose to illustrate the purposes and applications of the Declaration of Independence and the ideals that shaped our nation as we celebrate the 250th anniversary of this document this year. This may include its history, adoption, and recognition of significant individuals involved. Or they may focus on any concept contained in the Declaration of Independence. </p><p><strong>Theme Expansion Ideas:</strong></p><ul><li>Endowed with Liberty: 250 Years of the Declaration of Independence</li><li>Endowed by Their Creator: 250 Years of the Declaration of Independence</li><li>We Hold These Truths: Celebrating 250 Years of Civic Courage</li><li>Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness: 250 Years of the Declaration of Independence</li><li>A Foundation Built on Principles: Celebrating 250 Years of the Declaration of Independence</li><li>Consent of the Governed: Celebrating 250 Years of the Declaration of Independence</li><li>“We mutually pledge to each other our Lives, our Fortunes, and our sacred Honor”: 250 Years of the Declaration of Independence</li><li>When in the course of human events: 250 Years of the Declaration of Independence</li><li>Instituting New Government With Its Foundation Built on Principles: Celebrating 250 Years of the Declaration of Independence</li><li>Voices of Independence: Then, Now, Future</li></ul><p><b>All submissions must support the primary values of: <span style="font-style: inherit;">God, Family, Freedom, and Country</span></b></p><p><b><span style="font-style: inherit;">Website Resources:</span></b></p><ul><li><a href="https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs">Declaration of Independence, Bill of Rights, and the Constitution</a></li><li><a href="https://america250.utah.gov/education/">America 250 Utah (K-12 lesson plans)</a></li><li><a href="https://constitutioncenter.org/">National Constitution Center</a></li><li><a href="https://www.billofrightsinstitute.org/">Bill of Rights Institute</a></li><li><a href="https://civiced.org/we-the-people">Center for Civic Education</a></li><li>Center for Constitutional Studies, Utah Valley University: constitution@uvu.edu</li></ul>								</div>

									<div class="columnOne"><p><strong>Contest Rules</strong></p><ul><li>The Freedom Festival Essay Contest is open to ALL Students in grades K-12, whether in traditional public schools, public chartered schools, private schools, or home schools.</li><li>All entries must be received no later than March 1<strong>.</strong></li><li>All submitted essays must include a completed Contest Entry.  No personal or identifying information may appear on the essay itself.  (No names, grades, teachers’ names or school names on the essays.)</li><li>Winners will be notified by email when judging is completed.  Original essays will not be returned.</li></ul></div><div class="columnTwo"><p><strong>Judging Criteria</strong></p><p>Entries are judged on a student’s exposition of the theme, depth of insight, writing skill, sincerity of tone, and provided personal examples.  Essays must not exceed 900 words and may be type or hand written.
